correction.text: the Najahid emirate of Zabid in the Tihaman lowland; years 1067-1071 only (the Najahids are landless 1062-1066, the family at Dahlak)

keyframe_review.note: 215,442 km2 for 1066-1071. Cliopatria's Najahid shape is an all-Yemen union (Sa'dah to Aden and Shabwah, including Sana'a and Aden). Pages: the Najahids were 'in the Tihaman lowland' (Sulayhid page) with Zabid as capital (Najahid page infobox); the Sulayhids held Sana'a, Haraz and then Jibla until 1138 and the Zurayids held Aden from 1083 (Sulayhid and Zurayids pages). No page opened gives the Najahids more than Zabid and the Tihama. The Najahids are in exile at Dahlak from the Sulayhid capture of Zabid in 1062 ('forced Najah's children to flee to Dahlak', no year) until Sa'id Ibn Najah appears as 'the prince of Zabid' in 1067 (Zabid page), so the correction applies from 1067; 1062-1066 has no land.

correction.text: Zabid and the Tihaman lowland until Ali ibn Mahdi's conquest in 1158

keyframe_review.note: 212,580 km2 for 1152-1168. Cliopatria's Najahid shape is an all-Yemen union (Sa'dah to Aden and Shabwah, including Sana'a and Aden). Pages: the Najahids were 'in the Tihaman lowland' (Sulayhid page) with Zabid as capital (Najahid page infobox); the Sulayhids held Sana'a, Haraz and then Jibla until 1138 and the Zurayids held Aden from 1083 (Sulayhid and Zurayids pages). No page opened gives the Najahids more than Zabid and the Tihama. Zabid page: 'the slave dynasty came an end and the Mahdids took over Zabid in 1158'; Najahid page: 'Their last sovereign was killed by Ali ibn Mahdi the Kharijite in 1158'. The Najahid state therefore ends in 1158, ten years before Cliopatria's last year; 1159-1168 belongs to the Mahdids (Zabid page: 'the Mahdids (1158 to 1174)').

ledger.note: 1022: Najah, an Abyssinian administrator, founds the Najahid emirate at Zabid. Page: 'The last Ziyadid king died in 1018, leaving a child behind', the guardianship passed to a slave and the infobox has 'Established 1022'. The page gives the capital, not a boundary.

1062: the Sulayhids take Zabid and the Tihama; Najah's children flee to Dahlak. Ali page: his forces captured Zabid and the Tihamah 'later in 1062'; Sulayhid page: 'The ruler of the Najahids in the Tihaman lowland was poisoned in 1060 and his capital Zabid was taken by the Sulayhids'; Najahid page: 'forced Najah's children to flee to Dahlak' (no year).

1067: the Najahids are back at Zabid and kill Ali al-Sulayhi on the pilgrimage road. Zabid page: 'In 1067, during the pilgrimage to Mecca, the Banu Najah clan under Sa'id Ibn Najah, the prince of Zabid,' attacked Ali's party (the Ali page has 1066). No page dates the recapture of Zabid; 1067 is the first year the Najahids hold it.

region.text: Zabid and the Tihama, with the town of Asma

ledger.note: 1082: the Sulayhids take Zabid. Ali page: 'In 1082, al-Mukkaram led a Sulayhid force against Zabid, quickly capturing the city and Asma', forcing al-Ahwal to flee to the island of Dahlak. Review fix: the first draft typed this a contest_start.

1087: Said al-Ahwal comes back to Zabid. Najahid page: 'In 1087, Said al-Ahwal returned to Zabid but was killed that same year by Ahmed al-Mukkaram.' Whether the Najahids held the city is not on the page; the contest runs to 1089.
1089: the contest ends with the Najahids in Zabid. Najahid page: 'Jayyash returned to Zabid disguised as an Indian' (undated), Jayyash 1080-1089 and Fatiq ibn Jayyash 1089-1104.
1089 at the latest: the Najahids rule Zabid again (Najahid page: Jayyash's return, undated; Fatiq ibn Jayyash 1089-1104). Confidence 1: the page is silent on the year.

1158: the Mahdids take Zabid and the Najahid dynasty ends. Page: 'the slave dynasty came an end and the Mahdids took over Zabid in 1158'; Najahid page: 'Their last sovereign was killed by Ali ibn Mahdi the Kharijite in 1158'. Cliopatria keeps the Najahids to 1168.

wars.name: Sulayhid-Najahid wars
wars.outcome: The Sulayhids took Zabid in 1062; the Najahids killed Ali al-Sulayhi on the pilgrimage road (1066 or 1067) and were at Zabid again by 1067; al-Mukarram captured Zabid and Asma in 1082 and al-Ahwal fled to Dahlak; Said al-Ahwal returned in 1087 and was killed that year; Jayyash returned (undated) and the Najahids held Zabid by 1089.
wars.note: The Najahid page gives no year for any of these; the Zabid page dates Ali's death to 1067.

wars.name: Sulayhid-Zurayid siege of Zabid
wars.outcome: The Sulayhid leader al-Mufaddal besieged Zabid with the Zurayid brothers, who were killed in the siege; Zabid held.

wars.name: Mahdid conquest of Zabid
wars.outcome: Ali ibn Mahdi killed the last Najahid sovereign and the Mahdids took Zabid in 1158.
wars.note: Najahid page: killed by Ali ibn Mahdi 'the Kharijite' in 1158.

certainty.note: No boundary appears on any page; Zabid and the Tihama are named places. 1062-1066: no land (the family in exile at Dahlak).

notes:
Pages: the Najahid dynasty, Sulayhid dynasty, Ali al-Sulayhi, Zabid and Zurayids (budget 5); the Najahid page is nearly silent on territory.
Cliopatria faults: the six Najahid shapes (1066-1168) are an all-Yemen union or a northern-highland patch and contradict the pages (Sulayhids at Sana'a/Jibla, Zurayids at Aden); all six are marked wrong with the Tihama of Zabid as the correction. Cliopatria starts the Najahids in 1066 (the page: 1022) and ends them in 1168 (page: 1158). 1062-1066 is landless: Zabid was Sulayhid and the family sat at Dahlak.
The Najahid recovery of Zabid is undated: the Ali page has Zabid taken 'later in 1062', the Zabid page has Sa'id Ibn Najah 'the prince of Zabid' in 1067, the Najahid page lists Jayyash from 1080 and has Sa'id back in 1087 (killed the same year). The ledger records the loss in 1062, the gain in 1067, the loss in 1082 (Ali page: Zabid captured), the contest 1087-1089 and the gain in 1089 (confidence 1).
Cliopatria's Ziyadid row (866-1138, six shapes) overlaps the Najahids: the Najahid page says the last Ziyadid king died in 1018. Cliopatria's Mahdids row (1169-1506, 'centred on Oman') is not the Mahdids of Zabid (1158-1174).
Counterpart dossiers: sulayhid-dynasty (mine); mahdids (a Zabid Mahdid dossier may be needed, 1158-1174, group me-09 or me-08); ziyadid-dynasty (me-08).
Gazetteer names needed: Dahlak archipelago (Najahid refuge; unused here).
Review repair (2026-10-20): the Ali page (re-opened) says the Sulayhids captured Zabid in 1082 and al-Ahwal fled to Dahlak, so 1082 is a loss (confidence 3), not a contest; the Najahids hold no land 1082-1088 (correction text of the 1072 and 1085 keyframes); Said al-Ahwal's return and death in 1087 start a contest that ends in 1089 with Jayyash's undated return (Fatiq ibn Jayyash from 1089). The 1066 keyframe now reads 'years 1067-1071'. Kept in step with sulayhid-dynasty. Still not settled: the year of the first return to Zabid after 1062 (1067 at confidence 2) and any extent beyond Zabid and the Tihama.
